mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Screening and clearance completion report demonstrating no adverse hits on UN, OFAC, EU, and Egyptian national sanctions lists for all UBOs and directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered compliance service provider or corporate legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized declaration and legal cover letter; no apostille required if issued by a licensed Egyptian professional

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all founding members, UBOs, directors, authorized signatories, and counterparties against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Egyptian domestic terrorism financing list issued by the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit, and the Egyptian Central Bank of Egypt sanctions directives. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) must be identified and subjected to enhanced due diligence including source-of-funds verification, senior management approval, and ongoing monitoring under AML Law 80/2002 and EMLCU instructions. Negative screen results must be archived and available for inspection; any positive match requires immediate filing of a Suspicious Transaction Report with the EMLCU and the transaction must be blocked.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Investor Services e-System / Egyptian Company Registry Name Reservation Module at https://eservices.gafi.gov.eg
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name must be in Arabic and may include a transliterated Latin-script English name in parallel. Arabic grammar, orthography, and permissible word order apply; the registry uses the approved Arabic name as the strict legal corporate name, with the English version reserved for foreign documentation. Phonetic transliteration from Arabic to Latin must follow the Egyptian Ministry of Trade approved transliteration guide. Names that are misleading, inconsistent with the licensed activity, identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, or incapable of unambiguous transliteration are rejected. The name must end with 'LLC' or 'Limited Liability Company' in English and 'شركة ذات مسئولية محدودة' in Arabic.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection or deemed rejection, the applicant may submit an administrative appeal via the same GAFI e-services portal within 15 business days of the rejection notice, attaching an Arabic memorandum stating the grounds and a corrected version of the proposed name. The GAFI Companies Registry Appeal Committee must review and issue a written decision within 30 days of submission. If rejected, the applicant may request an extension of the original name reservation by filing a new reservation; a formal rejection does not alter the entity formation sequence and the applicant may resubmit with a revised distinctive name. An unsuccessful administrative appeal may be escalated to the competent Economic Court within 60 days of the GAFI decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as the sole registered office for an Egyptian LLC. The LLC must maintain a physical office address in Egypt, with a visible nameplate and capacity to receive legal process, correspondence, and government inspections. A serviced office or commercial office center with a physical desk and management office is permissible for a dredging/EPC contractor provided the office is operational on business days and the employer/oversight authorities can conduct inspections. A purely virtual or virtual-mailbox-only address is not acceptable under GAFI and Commercial Registry standards.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 25% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by GAFI, the Commercial Registry, the Tax Authority, or the AML supervisory authority within the first 24 months of operation, with an additional 15% annual likelihood for registered EPC contractors under construction and maritime license supervision. The office must comply with signage, recordkeeping, and employee presence requirements.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 148 of 2019 (LLC provisions); Executive Regulations of Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 1982, as amended); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018; Executive Regulations of Investment Law (Ministerial Decree No. 2310 of 2017); Ministry of Justice Notarization and Commercial Registry regulations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - One-Stop Shop, operating jointly with the Commercial Registry Office and the Ministry of Justice Notary Public, Cairo Governorate
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic Incorporation Application (GAFI 'Egypt for Startups' portal) together with the Contract of Incorporation and Articles of Association (Aqd Ta'sis / Nizam Asasi) executed in Arabic before a Notary Public
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Egyptian LLC; share capital is freely fixed in the Articles of Association and must be fully subscribed. In-kind contributions require valuation by a GAFI-approved valuer. No mandatory escrow bank account under company law, but the competent port authority may impose a dredging performance bond before commencing marine works.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: We, the founding partners of EG_LLC, hereby resolve: (1) the share capital is duly subscribed and allocated per the Articles of Association; (2) the registered office is fixed at the Cairo office stated in the Articles for all official correspondence; (3) the two founding partners are appointed joint managers, acting singly on administrative matters and jointly on contracts above USD 50,000; (4) such managers are authorized to complete commercial registration, tax, social-insurance, bank account opening, hiring, and all licensing applications under Egyptian law; (5) this resolution takes effect immediately and shall be filed with GAFI and the Commercial Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Legal Form Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop / 'Egypt for Startups' online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name reservation request for two candidate company names in Arabic and English. Complete the legal-form checklist confirming an LLC structure, proposed registered office address (lease or title deed), intended objects written to match ISIC 4290/NAICS 237990, and nationality/shareholding data for each founder. Obtain the GAFI name approval certificate before drafting the Articles.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application with two alternative names
Valid passport/ID copies of all founding partners
Certificate of good standing for any foreign corporate shareholder
Evidence of registered office address (lease or ownership contract)
Draft statement of objects aligned to marine dredging and seawall construction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, file two fresh alternatives immediately at the same counter; if the object clause is challenged, amend the objects wording and resubmit, with escalation review available within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Association and Execution of the Act of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice Notary Public Office, Cairo; licensed Egyptian attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a lawyer licensed before the Egyptian National Bar Association to draft the Arabic Contract of Incorporation and Articles of Association, including company name, objects, capital division, manager appointments, profit-sharing ratios, in-kind contribution valuations, dispute resolution clause, and registered office clause. Convene all founders before the Notary Public to sign and authenticate the document; ensure the Notary affixes the authentication number and page stamps.
required_dossiers: GAFI name approval certificate
Draft Articles of Association in Arabic
Valid IDs of all founding partners and their authorized signatories
Notarization fee payment receipt
Power of attorney authorizing the incorporation lawyer, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial defects, such as mismatch between company name and name approval, are cured by a supplementary amendment deed executed before the Notary; re-authentication does not restart the incorporation timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Incorporation Filing with GAFI One-Stop Shop and Fee Settlement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (OSS) - electronic filing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the notarized Arabic Articles, name approval certificate, capital subscription evidence, and OSS incorporation application form to the GAFI portal. Pay the official state filing fee (approximately USD 250 or EGP equivalent) by card or bank deposit. GAFI reviews the submission against Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and issues the incorporation decision with a provisional company ID and provisional commercial registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Association
GAFI name approval certificate
Bank certificate evidencing subscription proceeds or joint declaration of capital availability
Registered office lease or title deed proof
Completed OSS incorporation form with manager signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a defect sheet, submit all requested corrections within 3 business days; a final negative decision may be contested before the GAFI Dispute Settlement Committee under the Investment Law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Registration and Issuance of Commercial Registration Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Authority, Cairo Governorate branch, via GAFI OSS interface
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The GAFI OSS transmits the incorporation decision to the Commercial Registry. Present the notarized Articles, registered office proof, and manager specimen signatures; obtain the Commercial Registration Certificate (Sagil Togari), which establishes legal personality for bank account opening, tax registration, and contract signing.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation decision and provisional company ID
Notarized Articles of Association
Proof of registered office (lease or ownership)
Manager identity documents and specimen signature pages
Commercial Registry application fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address registry queries on the registered office by filing a rectification petition or amending the registered address through the GAFI OSS before certificate issuance; minor data mismatches are cured by a corrective declaration from the joint managers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration: Corporate Tax Card, VAT Certification, and Payroll Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - local tax directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for corporate income tax via the ETA electronic services platform using the Commercial Registration number. Apply for the tax card (Bitaka Da'ibia). Because marine dredging EPC revenues will exceed the mandatory threshold, complete VAT registration under Law No. 67 of 2016 at the standard rate of 14%. Register for payroll and stamp duty if local employees are hired after incorporation.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration certificate
Notarized Articles of Association
Company registered office lease contract
Bank certificate of subscribed capital
Manager identity documents and tax card application form
VAT registration form and forecast of taxable supplies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA issues a tax card data mismatch, resubmit with a supporting letter from the Commercial Registry; any contested VAT registration date may be objected before the ETA Appeals Committee within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Maritime Industry Licensing and EEAA Environmental Pre-Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Authority for Maritime Safety (EAMS) with the competent Port Authority; Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) regional office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After commercial and tax registration, submit the Dredging and Marine Construction Works Operating License application to EAMS, including company legal documents, equipment list, dredging methodology, and vessel class certificates. Simultaneously file the EEAA environmental screening form describing dredged volumes, work locations, and disposal or reclamation sites. After license approval, register the company on the relevant Port Authority vendor list and submit the Civil Defense clearance for the onshore base.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation certificate and Commercial Registration certificate
Tax card and VAT certificate
Dredger/vessel registration and classification society certificates
Planned equipment list and dredging methodology statement
EEAA preliminary EIA screening form
Civil Defense fire-safety approval for shore base facilities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If EAMS issues technical objections, supply certified class-survey reports and revised method statements and resubmit; if EEAA assigns Category C full EIA, engage an approved EIA consultant and coordinate the public participation process; adverse environmental permit conditions may be grieved before the EEAA grievance committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Egyptian Authority for Maritime Safety (EAMS) - Licensing and Registration Sector, Ministry of Transport, in coordination with the landlord Port Authority (e.g., Suez Canal Authority for SCZone waters, Alexandria Port Authority, Damietta Port Authority, or Safaga Port Authority) that controls the project site
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Dredging and Marine Construction Works Operating License (Rukhsat A'mal Al-Takreeb wa Al-Insha'at Al-Bahriya), including contractor classification for civil marine works under ISIC 4290

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) - Environmental Impact Assessment Central Department, Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C (Full EIA Report) for capital dredging, seawall or breakwater construction, and dredged material disposal in sensitive coastal zones; Category B (Limited Environmental Study) for smaller maintenance dredging outside sensitive areas; screening tier is confirmed by the EEAA Preliminary Screening Letter
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 4 of 1994 as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009 and its Executive Regulations: no oil sheen; total suspended solids (TSS) in overflow wastewater ≤ 30 mg/L; dredged sediment must satisfy Egyptian marine sediment quality criteria for TPH, heavy metals, and PCBs before offshore disposal; construction equipment emissions must conform to Egyptian ambient air standards for PM, NOx, and SO2; noise ≤ 70 dB(A) at the nearest habitation; continuous turbidity monitoring required near reefs and sensitive receptors during hopper overflow and bottom discharge

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense (Al-Himaya Al-Madaniya) fire safety and emergency response certification for the onshore base, workshops, and worker camps; structural load inspection approval for cranes, temporary marine platforms, and jack-up equipment; occupational health and workplace clearance under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003, including medical fitness certificates for offshore crews; ISPS-compliant port access clearance and dredge vessel seaworthiness certification by an authorized classification society; dredge spoil disposal permit from the competent Port Authority

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; registration and electronic tax services are administered through the ETA electronic tax portal at eta.gov.eg and related unified tax registration systems.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate or register the Egyptian limited liability company, branch, or permanent establishment with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones or other competent registry, as applicable. 2. Obtain the commercial registration, constitutional documents, proof of registered address, and authorized-signatory documentation. 3. File the corporate tax registration application with the competent ETA office or through the ETA electronic portal. 4. Submit identification documents for the authorized representative, tax agent, and relevant foreign shareholders or directors where requested. 5. Register the entity for value-added tax when the statutory threshold is exceeded or when mandatory registration applies to the activity. 6. Obtain the Egyptian tax registration number and tax card; VAT registrants additionally obtain VAT registration confirmation and the applicable VAT registration number. 7. Enroll in the ETA electronic invoicing system where mandatory, complete electronic signature and technical onboarding requirements, and register required ERP or API integrations. 8. Register with Egyptian Customs and obtain the required customs importer/exporter credentials for export or import transactions. A nonresident supplying taxable goods or services in Egypt generally requires an Egyptian tax representative or other locally compliant registration arrangement, subject to the applicable VAT and procedural rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not generally provide a United States-style check-the-box election for a limited liability company. An Egyptian LLC is ordinarily subject to entity-level corporate income tax and VAT rules. Tax treatment may instead vary by legally distinct form, permanent-establishment status, approved investment or free-zone regime, or qualifying special economic-zone incentive; these are statutory classifications or incentive applications, not elective pass-through classifications. No general hybrid-mismatch election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT), administered under Egypt's Value Added Tax Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable turnover is the principal VAT registration threshold for taxable persons, subject to compulsory-registration rules, sector-specific provisions, and rules applicable to nonresident suppliers and imported services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt has a mandatory electronic invoicing framework for in-scope business-to-business transactions and other covered taxpayers, implemented in phases by the ETA. Taxpayers must register on the ETA electronic invoicing platform, use approved electronic invoicing software or API integration, apply a qualified electronic signature or approved digital-signature method, generate the prescribed invoice data and unique identifier, and submit invoices for ETA validation or clearance in accordance with the applicable phase. Electronic receipts apply to covered business-to-consumer transactions under the ETA e-receipt framework. Invoices must contain prescribed supplier, customer, tax, supply, and payment information; unregistered, rejected, or technically noncompliant documents may jeopardize input VAT deduction and expense support.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Egypt to a destination outside Egypt may qualify for VAT at 0% where the export is completed through the prescribed customs process and the supplier retains documentary evidence of export, supply value, and payment. Exported services may qualify for zero rating only where they satisfy the statutory definition and conditions for services exported outside Egypt, including the relevant place-of-supply, recipient, use, and payment requirements. Services physically performed or economically consumed in Egypt, including many construction, dredging, engineering, and port-related activities performed in Egypt, should not be treated as exported services merely because the customer is nonresident. Zero-rating and VAT refunds require consistent invoices, customs records, accounting records, and banking evidence; unsupported claims may be reassessed as domestic taxable supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration accepted and finalized by Egyptian Customs
Commercial export invoice identifying the Egyptian supplier, foreign consignee, goods, value, currency, and delivery terms
Packing list and cargo or shipment documentation
Bill of lading, airway bill, or other transport document evidencing shipment outside Egypt
Customs exit, release, or proof-of-export evidence showing physical departure from Egypt
Foreign-currency bank receipt, inward-remittance evidence, or other acceptable proof of consideration, where required for the relevant transaction or refund file
Contracts, purchase orders, certificates of completion, and delivery or acceptance records supporting the exported supply
VAT invoices and electronic-invoice records containing the required ETA data and unique identifiers
Import-country or destination evidence where requested by ETA or customs authorities
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA may deny zero rating or a VAT refund and assess the applicable domestic VAT, statutory late-payment additions, and administrative penalties where export, payment, customs-exit, invoicing, or service-export conditions are not substantiated. Refunds paid on the basis of inaccurate, incomplete, fictitious, or duplicated documentation may be recovered with applicable additions and may trigger audit reassessment. Failure to register, issue compliant invoices, maintain records, file returns, or use the required electronic systems may attract penalties under the VAT Law and related tax procedures. Deliberate tax evasion, concealment of taxable turnover, fabrication of export documents, false refund claims, or collusion may constitute criminal tax offenses, exposing responsible persons and entities to fines, imprisonment, cancellation or suspension of tax privileges, and referral to prosecution. The 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation period should be treated as the required transaction-control deadline for this dossier; the precise FX evidence and timing must be verified against the applicable banking, customs, export-control, contract, and ETA requirements for the transaction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - Foreign Exchange Administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Egyptian Pound (EGP) is classified as a partially convertible currency. Current account transactions, including import payments and service fees, may be routed through authorized banks without prior CBE approval provided underlying trade documentation is presented. Capital account transactions, notably shareholder equity injections, foreign loans, and repatriation of investment proceeds, are subject to mandatory registration with the CBE and tax clearance certificates issued by the Egyptian Tax Authority. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted only after filing audited financial statements and settling any corporate tax liabilities, with documented proof of the source of funds for the original investment. Offshore foreign currency accounts maintained locally are subject to aggregate balance limits and are not freely transferable without a valid underlying transaction payment order.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export proceeds, including servicing contracts for maritime dredging and breakwater works, must be repatriated to Egypt within 30 days from the date of shipment or completion of the monthly progress milestone, as certified by the competent port authority. The full amount of proceeds received in convertible foreign currency must be offered for sale to an authorized banking dealer within five banking days of credit to the exporter's foreign currency account. Mandatory conversion to EGP is applicable to the entire proceeds at the weighted average market rate, unless the entity holds a valid CBE general authorization to retain a percentage for trade-related operational expenditures, which for dredging sector services, does not exceed 20% of invoiced value. The entity must submit a shipping bill, signed contract, invoicing certificate, and an escrow confirmation from the project owner to the authorized bank for each repatriation and sale transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_additional_not: For services rendered to a sovereign port authority, the contractual milestone certificate is treated as the shipping equivalent, and the 30-day period commences upon issuance and certification of the project milestone by the owner.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low with a strict legal prohibition. Offshore fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not recognized as licensed banks in Egypt and cannot provide domestic or foreign currency accounts to Egyptian legal entities. Any entity that accepts payments on behalf of the Egyptian company would violate CBE Banking Law No. 194 of 2020 and could result in account freeze, statutory penalties, and administrative sanctions. A licensed Egyptian Fintech partner could act solely as a payment gateway for project collections from third parties, but only if the final settlement is routed into a CBE-licensed commercial bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Egyptian banks universally require the physical presence of at least one authorized director, the designated signatory, and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) for an in-person interview during the account opening procedure. Remote opening is not permitted for non-resident-owned limited liability companies without a prior existing banking relationship of at least two years with the same Egyptian bank and a formal notarized power of attorney executed at the Egyptian Consulate. The company must produce original certified constituent documents (certified by the Egyptian General Authority for Investment - GAFI), commercial registry extract, tax card, Chamber of Commerce registration, and board resolution authorizing the account signatories. A notarized and consular-legalized copy of the UBO passport and the board resolution are mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate shareholders domiciled in a high-risk jurisdiction or a jurisdiction on the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) grey list
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate ownership legalization chain (certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, register of directors and UBO of each intermediate entity), audited financial statements of the shareholder for the last three years, source-of-wealth declaration, notarized passport copies of each UBO, and a professional independent reference letter from a licensed global bank operating in the shareholder's jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dredging and maritime infrastructure contracts with the public sector, raising undue scrutiny on potential bribery or misappropriation of public funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed EPC contract with the port authority or sovereign entity, finalized tender and award minutes, commercial invoice, project valuation certificate, official registration in the Egyptian Federation of Contractors, and an integrity and anti-corruption compliance undertaking signed by the entity's managers, supported by internationally accepted corporate anti-bribery policies (including clear no-commission/no-agent clauses).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injections exceeding the minimum share capital or investor-specific funding that is not clearly justified by the business plan
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed project budget and cash flow forecast indicating the deployment of funds, written board resolution from the Egyptian company approving the capital injection, validated share subscription form, bank reference letters for the remitting institution, anti-money laundering source-of-funds questionnaire, and tax registration certificate evidencing future tax exposure of capital is fully disclosed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The company's operational activity involves high-value international wire transfers to equipment suppliers deemed as high maritime risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier technical dossier (company registration, financial accounts, IMO-related compliance, and sanctions list screening), proforma invoice, Bill of Lading or airway bill, certificate of origin, pre-shipment inspection certificate, fully executed vessel charterparty or equipment purchase agreement, and a transaction-by-transaction economic substance memorandum prepared by a licensed accountant.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_alternative_route: If physical presence of the UBO cannot be arranged, the company may appoint a resident Egyptian manager with a written notarized power of attorney and a board resolution granting full banking authority; however, the bank will still require a video-call conference with the non-resident director and authenticate the notarized documents from the Egyptian diplomatic mission in the director's jurisdiction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections from foreign shareholders must be routed through an authorized dealer bank in Egypt using a SWIFT MT103 wire transfer with the clearly stated purpose code and narrative referencing the investment registration certificate or project approval from GAFI and the Central Bank of Egypt. The remitting bank must receive a certified board resolution of the Egyptian entity and the executed notarized share subscription agreement. The funds must be credited to a special foreign currency Investment Account opened by the Egyptian entity; the ratio of conversion of the injected funds into EGP is optional, subject to the CBE's market rate. The beneficiary bank must register the operation in the CBE's electronic transfer order system within one business day and obtain a transfer order confirmation. For amounts exceeding a threshold imposed by CBE regulations (approximately USD 1 million or equivalent), the entity must submit a source-of-funds declaration to the compliance officer, together with the apostilled certificate of incorporation and board minutes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for trade and operating expenses (fuel, submarine equipment, maintenance imports, port state dues) must be cleared via SWIFT MT103 for amounts below USD 1,000,000 and via a documentary commercial letter of credit for larger amounts. All foreign payments must be supported with a valid proforma invoice, port authority contract, service agreement, customs declaration, tax certificate, and prior import approval when applicable. Authorized banks will perform a purpose-code screening and, where required, confirm settlement with the CBE's electronic payment approval gateway. Same-day clearing is available only for payments to sanctioned-free, high-income jurisdictions with a strong banking relationship; otherwise, the settlement cycle ranges from two to five business days. For dredging mobilization and charter payment to foreign vessels, a charterparty and a technical authorization from the maritime authority must be appended to the payment file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain Vanilla FX Forward contracts (delivery-based, non-deliverable forward not permitted for local EGP receivable) with a tenor not exceeding twelve months and a documented underlying trade or service transaction
FX/Currency Swaps with an authorized bank designated as a market-maker, used exclusively for matching two transactional currency cash flows (e.g., USD receivable and USD payable)
Local EGP/USD OTC Forward with mandatory underlying export/import documentary support, entered into only with a CBE-licensed dealing bank at a transparent forward margin

Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) when borrowing is undertaken for the dredging project and the swap directly converts a fixed-rate EGP liability into USD floating-rate liability with actual principal exchange at maturity
Repo contracts in Egyptian Treasury bills denominated in EGP as a collateralized liquidity hedge for short-term local operational working capital, not as a standalone speculative instrument
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.hedging_note: Currency options are not listed as permissible hedging instruments due to Egyptian regulatory constraints; a practical hedge is achieved through a matching schedule of export proceeds and payable obligations rather than exotic derivative products.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Register Renewal (Trade Register certificate)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Commercial Register / GAFI One-Stop Shop, Ministry of Trade & Industry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every calendar year during January (January 1 – January 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-renewal penalty EGP 500–10,000 (approx. USD 10–210); non-renewal for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off from the Commercial Register and loss of legal standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Card (Tax Identification Card) Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Tax Registration Department at the competent local tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in January; card expires at end of January and renewal must be completed within the January renewal window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine EGP 1,000–5,000 for operating with an expired tax card; blocked bank, notary, port-authority and government-tender clearances; possible license suspension.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 19) with audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Central Corporate Taxation Department (e-filing; Large Taxpayer Center where applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 30 for calendar-year taxpayers (within four months of the fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine EGP 3,000–50,000 under Art. 136 of Income Tax Law 91/2005; additional 1% monthly late-payment surcharge on unpaid tax; enforced bank attachment and collection measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Payroll / Salary Tax Final Settlement (Form 41) and monthly withholding returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Payroll and Withholding Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly withholding returns by the 15th of the following month; annual payroll final settlement by the last day of February of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same statutory fine band of EGP 3,000–50,000 per delinquent filing; unpaid payroll tax may be reassessed with collection surcharge and may expose LLC managers to personal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AGM approval of audited financial statements and filing with GAFI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop / Companies Registry; copy delivered to the Commercial Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held within six months of the fiscal year-end; GAFI filing within 30 days of AGM approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine EGP 10,000–50,000 imposed on the LLC and its managers; GAFI certificates and services restricted; omission of annual filings for two consecutive years exposes the company to administrative strike-off or judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Confirmation and share-transfer notifications
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI – Companies Registration and AML Compliance Unit (UBO register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the audited financial statements; any UBO or shareholding change reported to GAFI within 30 days; quota transfers also registered in the Commercial Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine EGP 20,000–200,000 under Anti-Money Laundering Law 80/2002 and Cabinet Decree 15/2020; refusal of GAFI and notarial clearance for share transfers; AML registration freeze.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory register audit and on-site records verification (members, managers, minutes, transfers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records maintained at the Egyptian registered office; subject to GAFI and ETA inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous maintenance with annual validation at the AGM and on-demand production to inspectors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine EGP 5,000–20,000 for defective or incomplete statutory registers; managers may be barred from public procurement and port-authority contracting lists.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all LLCs under Companies Law 159/1981 irrespective of size: every LLC must appoint an ETA-accredited statutory auditor. For tax purposes, audited financial statements are additionally required for companies with gross turnover above EGP 3 million; a maritime dredging EPC entity holding port contracts normally exceeds this threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) fully converged with IFRS; large entities apply full IFRS-converged EAS, while SMEs may apply the simplified EAS for SMEs. Maritime dredging and rubble-mound breakwater revenue is recognized under IFRS 15 using percentage-of-completion and milestone methods.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must keep an updated UBO register at its Egyptian registered office and file an annual UBO confirmation with GAFI together with the audited financial statements. Any quota (share) transfer must be notarized, recorded in the Commercial Register, and notified to GAFI within 30 days; the annual confirmation serves as the certified year-end snapshot of the full ownership chain.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Minutes and Resolutions (Minute Book)
Register of Share Transfers and Pledges

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $800 – $1,800 per year (GAFI-registered agent, Cairo registered office, tax card and commercial register handling)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $1,200 – $3,500 per year (ETA-accredited mid-tier audit firm for an LLC holding maritime dredging EPC receivables)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% (standard Egyptian national corporate income tax rate under Law No. 91 of 2005 on Income Tax, as amended; special rates apply to banks at 40%, telecommunications at 40%, and petroleum/Suez Canal concessionary activities at 40.55%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 grants qualifying infrastructure and construction projects a deduction from taxable income of up to 50% of the actual invested capital in new marine dredging and breakwater assets, generally over a maximum of 7 years, subject to GAFI registration and annual capital-expenditure verification; projects licensed within the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) may elect the free-zone final levy regime of 1% (goods) or 5% (services) of annual revenues in lieu of standard CIT; accelerated depreciation is available for hopper dredgers, booster pumps, and heavy marine equipment; Law No. 152 of 2020 simplified SME cash-basis rates (turnover below EGP 20 million) are not available to this large-scale EPC contractor profile.
